nodes.description: Biallelic CSGALNACT1 variants remove or reduce CSGalNAcT-1 activity. The three missense alleles tested (p.Pro384Arg, p.Asp432Tyr, p.Asn264Ser) each show reduced N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase activity in vitro; the frameshift and start-codon-deleting alleles are presumed null. CSGalNAcT-1 transfers the first GalNAc residue to the glucuronic acid of the GlcA-Gal-Gal-Xyl linker tetrasaccharide, the step that commits a proteoglycan linker to chondroitin sulfate rather than heparan sulfate.

nodes.description: Fewer chondroitin/dermatan sulfate chains are initiated on proteoglycan core proteins. In patient fibroblasts the number of CS/DS chains is reduced while total CS/DS disaccharide content is, unexpectedly, increased, and heparan sulfate is also altered, consistent with fewer but longer chains and with linker substrate shifting toward heparan sulfate. Csgalnact1-null mouse cartilage has about half the normal CS with normal chain length. A 2017 study found no difference in proteoglycan synthesis in the first patient's fibroblasts or in urinary GAG content, so the fibroblast chain-number finding depends on the assay used. The authors propose that the paralogue CSGalNAcT-2 compensates in part, which would explain the mild phenotype.
